expected_behavior: The start-bit wait counter is loaded with 11 instead of 10, so the receiver waits one extra bit period before sampling the first data bit.
exposing_condition: Send one valid byte; all data bits are sampled one bit period late, so the received byte is corrupted.

expected_behavior: The receiver clears its output-valid flag whenever the sink is ready, even if the sink never actually accepted the pending byte, so an unaccepted byte is silently dropped.
exposing_condition: Assert m_axis_tready before or while m_axis_tvalid is still low/pending acceptance; the byte in flight is discarded and never delivered.

expected_behavior: Reset polarity is inverted: the module holds itself in reset while rst is low and runs its normal state machine while rst is asserted, so registers never get a clean start-up value.
exposing_condition: Release reset (rst=0) with rxd idle-high; the counter/FIFO state is stale instead of cleared and the receiver misinterprets the idle line, producing a spurious or corrupted byte.

expected_behavior: The bit counter is loaded with 8 instead of 9, so the transmitter emits one fewer bit per frame and the stop-bit timing is shifted one bit period early.
exposing_condition: Transmit any byte; the frame is one bit short, so the receiving side sees the stop bit in the wrong slot and detects a framing error on every byte.

expected_behavior: The LSB-first shift register shifts in a 1 instead of a 0 on the left, corrupting the bit stream in the upper data bits of every transmitted frame.
exposing_condition: Transmit any byte with any bit set in the upper half (e.g. 8'hF0); the received byte differs from the transmitted one.

expected_behavior: Ready is forced high immediately when a byte is accepted instead of being gated to deassert while the shifter is loading, so a back-to-back write on the same cycle can overwrite data_reg mid-load.
exposing_condition: Keep s_axis_tvalid asserted continuously; the second byte is accepted one cycle earlier than the design intends, corrupting the currently shifting frame's data.
